Ticket 08 investigation (fake `git` genuinely absent from PATH, via path_exclusive: true -- an empty leading PATH entry alone does not hide a real git further down an inherited PATH). The pinned Oracle's own `import git` (deps/github_downloader.py:16, deps/bare_cache.py:34) runs GitPython's mandatory import-time refresh (git/__init__.py:263-298, git/cmd.py Git.refresh:741-905), which shells out to a bare `git version` before the Oracle's own CLI dispatch -- and hence doctor.py's own try/except FileNotFoundError (doctor.py:112-140) -- ever runs. When git is genuinely absent, that probe raises GitCommandNotFound, Git.refresh's default GIT_PYTHON_REFRESH="raise" mode converts it to ImportError, and the whole Oracle CLI dies with an unhandled Python traceback (confirmed empirically by running the pinned Oracle directly) instead of ever reaching run_doctor. apm-go has no such import-time git dependency -- its checkGit only shells out inside runDoctor itself -- so it renders its normal table with both critical rows [x] and exits 1: the SAME exit code the Oracle's crash happens to produce, but on a completely different stdout/stderr. `error_body` (ticket 10's first-non-blank-line comparator) also differs as a direct consequence: the Oracle's is the traceback's own first line (its stdout is empty, so errorBody falls through to stderr), apm-go's is its table's title line "Environment Diagnostics" (its stdout is the whole table). This is an Oracle-side precondition failure (GitPython's own import-time contract, not something doctor.py chose), not a gap in apm-go's doctor implementation to fix; apm-go's clean behaviour is an intentional, recorded deviation. `exit_code` is deliberately NOT waived: both sides exit 1.
